key_insight: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold networks learn hyperelastic behavior from heterogeneous experiments and yield compact, closed-form strain energies through pruning and symbolic regression.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on expert-selected constitutive laws and multiple homogeneous tests while producing interpretable material models for finite element analysis.
method: Embed a constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold network in finite element model updating.
Fit measured kinematic fields and reaction forces from heterogeneous loading.
Prune and symbolically regress the network into a constitutively admissible strain energy.
evidence_signal: Experiments show 1–2% median displacement errors and transfer to a withheld hole pattern in rubber, few-percent profile and force agreement in silicone, and prediction of an inflated aortic specimen’s 3D shape.
watch_item: Transfer across hole patterns is demonstrated, but reliability under loading modes outside the calibration experiment remains to be established.
paper_title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
